Reliable systems need more than confidence. They need independent checks that fail differently.

## Evidence

The [Example Project](https://example.com/project) compared two review paths. **Independent Review** found assumptions that repeated inspection missed. This is a representative paragraph with enough prose to make deterministic excerpts useful without relying on an external service. It explains the observation, offers context, and gives the generator material for a concise social draft.

```python
print("code should not become an excerpt")
```

The practical lesson is to design verification as another instrument rather than an echo. Teams can test this by tracking which review path finds each class of defect. The result should be treated as evidence, not as proof that one tool is universally better. Different projects will expose different error correlations. Measurement should guide the workflow. The system should also remain easy to inspect. Clear boundaries make experiments easier to repeat. Explicit assumptions make disagreement useful. A small controlled trial is better than an unexamined rollout. Finally, record failures as carefully as successes so later decisions have a representative history.
